name: Signature
type_signature: L = (constants, function symbols with arities, relation symbols with arities)
description: A signature (language) is a set of constant symbols, function symbols, and relation symbols each equipped with an arity.

name: Domain (universe)
type_signature: dom(A) = |A|
description: The domain or universe of a structure is the underlying set on which its functions and relations are defined.

name: Cardinality of a structure
type_signature: |A| = card(dom(A))
description: The cardinality of a structure is the cardinality of its domain.

name: Term
type_signature: Term ::= variable | constant | f(t_1,...,t_n)
description: A term is a syntactic expression built from variables and constants by repeated application of function symbols.

name: Term function (value of a term)
type_signature: t^A : A^n → A
description: The term function is the map sending an assignment of domain elements to variables to the value the term takes under that assignment in the structure.

name: Homomorphism
type_signature: h : A → B preserving functions and relations
description: A homomorphism is a map between structures of the same signature that commutes with all function symbols and preserves all relation symbols.

name: Isomorphism
type_signature: f : A → B bijective with f, f^{-1} embeddings
description: An isomorphism is a bijective homomorphism whose inverse is also a homomorphism, so it preserves and reflects all functions and relations.

name: Substructure generated by a set
type_signature: ⟨X⟩_A = smallest substructure of A containing X
description: The substructure generated by a subset X is the smallest substructure containing X, consisting of all values of terms with parameters in X.

name: Reduct and expansion
type_signature: A↾L' (reduct), B (expansion) with L ⊆ L'
description: A reduct is a structure obtained by forgetting some symbols of the signature, and its expansion is a structure on the same domain interpreting additional symbols.

name: Diagram (atomic/literal)
type_signature: Diag(A) = set of atomic and negated-atomic sentences true in A_A
description: The diagram of a structure is the set of all atomic and negated atomic sentences with parameters that hold in the structure expanded by names for its elements.

name: Canonical (term) structure
type_signature: structure with domain = (closed terms)/~
description: A canonical or term structure is a structure whose elements are equivalence classes of closed terms, used in Henkin-style constructions.

name: First-order formula
type_signature: φ ::= atomic | ¬φ | φ∧ψ | ∃x φ
description: A first-order formula is a syntactic expression built from atomic formulas using boolean connectives and quantification over individual variables.

name: Atomic formula
description: An atomic formula is a relation symbol or equality applied to terms, with no connectives or quantifiers.

name: Free and bound variables
type_signature: free(φ) ⊆ Var, bound by quantifiers
description: A variable occurrence is bound if it lies within the scope of a quantifier binding it and free otherwise.

name: Sentence
type_signature: φ with free(φ) = ∅
description: A sentence is a first-order formula with no free variables.

name: Parametrically definable set
type_signature: {ā ∈ A^n : A ⊨ φ(ā,b̄)} for parameters b̄
description: A parametrically definable set is the solution set in a structure of a formula allowing parameters from the domain.

name: Theory of a structure Th(A)
type_signature: Th(A) = { sentences φ : A ⊨ φ }
description: The theory of a structure is the set of all first-order sentences true in it.

name: Elementary equivalence
type_signature: A ≡ B ⟺ Th(A) = Th(B)
description: Two structures are elementarily equivalent when they satisfy exactly the same first-order sentences.

name: Elementary embedding
type_signature: f : A → B with A ⊨ φ(ā) ⟺ B ⊨ φ(f ā)
description: An elementary embedding is a map between structures that preserves the truth of all first-order formulas with parameters.

name: Elementary Diagram Lemma
type_signature: B ⊨ ElDiag(A) ⟺ ∃ elementary embedding A → B↾L
description: The elementary diagram lemma states that models of the elementary diagram of a structure correspond exactly to its elementary extensions (up to elementary embedding).

name: Back-and-forth equivalence (potential isomorphism)
type_signature: A ≅_p B via a nonempty set of partial isomorphisms with back-and-forth property
description: Back-and-forth equivalence (potential isomorphism) holds between two structures when there is a nonempty family of partial isomorphisms closed under extending any member by one element on either side.

name: Cantor's theorem on DLO
type_signature: any two countable DLOs are isomorphic
description: Cantor's theorem states that any two countable dense linear orders without endpoints are isomorphic.

name: Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé game
type_signature: EF_n(A,B): n-round Spoiler/Duplicator pebble game
description: The Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé game is a two-player game of n rounds in which Duplicator must maintain a partial isomorphism against Spoiler's element choices in two structures.

name: Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé theorem
type_signature: Duplicator wins EF_n(A,B) ⟺ A ≡_n B
description: The Ehrenfeucht–Fraïssé theorem states that Duplicator has a winning strategy in the n-round game exactly when the two structures agree on all sentences of quantifier rank at most n.

name: Quantifier rank
type_signature: qr(φ) ∈ ℕ
description: The quantifier rank of a formula is the maximal depth of nesting of quantifiers occurring in it.

name: Hintikka formulas
type_signature: φ^n_ā : formula of quantifier rank n describing the n-type of ā
description: Hintikka formulas are the finitely many formulas of a given quantifier rank that completely describe a tuple up to back-and-forth equivalence of that rank.

name: Age of a structure
type_signature: Age(A) = { finitely generated B : B embeds in A } (up to iso)
description: The age of a structure is the class of all finitely generated structures that embed into it.

name: Hereditary property (HP)
type_signature: B ∈ K and A embeds in B ⟹ A ∈ K
description: A class has the hereditary property when it is closed under taking finitely generated substructures.

name: Joint embedding property (JEP)
type_signature: ∀A,B∈K ∃C∈K with A,B ↪ C
description: A class has the joint embedding property when any two of its members embed into a common member.

name: Amalgamation property (AP)
type_signature: A↪B, A↪C ⟹ ∃D with B↪D, C↪D agreeing on A
description: A class has the amalgamation property when any two extensions of a common member can be embedded into a single member compatibly over that member.

name: Fraïssé limit
type_signature: unique countable ultrahomogeneous M with Age(M) = K
description: The Fraïssé limit of a suitable class is the unique countable ultrahomogeneous structure whose age is that class.

name: Ultrahomogeneous structure
type_signature: every iso between finitely generated substructures extends to an automorphism
description: A structure is ultrahomogeneous when every isomorphism between finitely generated substructures extends to an automorphism of the whole structure.

name: Fraïssé's theorem
type_signature: K with HP,JEP,AP,countably many iso types ⟹ unique Fraïssé limit
description: Fraïssé's theorem states that a countable class closed under isomorphism with HP, JEP, and AP has a unique countable ultrahomogeneous structure as its limit.

name: Weak homogeneity
type_signature: finite partial isos extend one element at a time
description: Weak homogeneity is the property that any isomorphism between finitely generated substructures can be extended to include any one further element.

name: The random graph (Rado graph)
type_signature: Fraïssé limit of finite graphs
description: The random graph is the unique countable graph that is the Fraïssé limit of all finite graphs and satisfies the extension property.

name: Extension property (graphs)
type_signature: ∀ disjoint finite U,V ∃z adjacent to all of U, none of V
description: The extension property states that for any two disjoint finite sets of vertices there is another vertex joined to all of the first set and none of the second.

name: ℵ₀-categoricity of the random graph
type_signature: Th(random graph) is ℵ₀-categorical
description: The theory of the random graph is ℵ₀-categorical, having a unique countable model up to isomorphism.

name: Orbit and stabiliser
type_signature: orbit G·a, stabiliser G_a = {g : g·a = a}
description: For a group acting on a structure, the orbit of an element is its image set under the group and the stabiliser is the subgroup fixing it.

name: Permutation group topology
type_signature: basic open sets = cosets of pointwise stabilisers of finite tuples
description: The topology of pointwise convergence on a permutation group has as basic open sets the cosets of pointwise stabilisers of finite tuples.

name: Closed-subgroup characterization of automorphism groups
type_signature: G ≤ Sym(Ω) closed ⟺ G = Aut(A) for some structure A on Ω
description: A subgroup of the symmetric group on a set is the automorphism group of some structure exactly when it is closed in the topology of pointwise convergence.

name: k-homogeneity / k-transitivity
type_signature: G acts transitively on k-tuples (of distinct elements)
description: A permutation group is k-transitive when it acts transitively on ordered k-tuples of distinct elements, and k-homogeneous when transitive on k-element subsets.

name: Imaginary elements
type_signature: classes ā/E for ∅-definable equivalence relations E
description: Imaginary elements are equivalence classes of definable equivalence relations on tuples, adjoined to a structure to name quotients.

name: Small index property
type_signature: every subgroup of index < 2^ℵ0 is open
description: A countable structure has the small index property when every subgroup of its automorphism group of index less than the continuum is open.

name: Interpretation Γ
type_signature: Γ : A ⤳ B via definable domain, relations, and quotient
description: An interpretation of one structure in another is given by a definable subset, definable relations on it, and a definable equivalence relation whose quotient recovers the target structure.

name: Coordinate map
type_signature: f_Γ : (definable subset of A^n) ↠ B
description: The coordinate map of an interpretation is the definable surjection from the interpreting definable set onto the domain of the interpreted structure.

name: Reduction of theories via interpretation
description: Interpretation reduces questions about the interpreted structure (such as decidability or definability) to corresponding questions about the interpreting structure.

name: A^eq / M^eq construction
type_signature: A^eq = A with all imaginary sorts adjoined
description: The A^eq construction expands a structure by adding a sort for every ∅-definable equivalence relation together with the canonical projection maps.

name: Elimination of imaginaries
type_signature: every imaginary is interdefinable with a real tuple
description: A theory eliminates imaginaries when every definable equivalence class has a definable canonical representative as a tuple of real elements.

name: Pseudo-elementary class (PC)
type_signature: reducts of models of a theory in a larger signature
description: A pseudo-elementary class is the class of reducts to a signature of the models of a theory in a larger signature.

name: Word construction interpreting groups/fields
description: The word construction interprets a group or field inside a structure by encoding its elements and operations as definable words or coordinate tuples.

name: Gödel completeness theorem
type_signature: T ⊨ φ ⟺ T ⊢ φ
description: The completeness theorem states that a first-order sentence is a semantic consequence of a theory if and only if it is provable from it.

name: Direct and reduced product
type_signature: ∏A_i and (∏A_i)/F for a filter F
description: The direct product of structures is their coordinatewise product, and the reduced product modulo a filter identifies tuples agreeing on a set in the filter.

name: Compactness via ultraproducts
function_signature: (finitely satisfiable theory T) → (model of T as ultraproduct)
description: This technique proves the compactness theorem by building a model of a finitely satisfiable theory as an ultraproduct of models of its finite subsets.

name: Diagonal embedding into an ultrapower
type_signature: d : A → A^I/U, a ↦ [constant a]
description: The diagonal embedding sends each element of a structure to the class of the constant sequence, giving an elementary embedding into any ultrapower.

name: Łoś–Tarski preservation theorem
type_signature: φ preserved under substructures ⟺ φ equivalent to a universal sentence
description: The Łoś–Tarski theorem states that a first-order sentence is preserved under substructures if and only if it is logically equivalent to a universal sentence.

name: Chang–Łoś–Suszko theorem
type_signature: φ preserved under unions of chains ⟺ equivalent to ∀∃ sentence
description: The Chang–Łoś–Suszko theorem states that a sentence is preserved under unions of chains if and only if it is equivalent to a universal-existential (∀∃) sentence.

name: Lyndon's preservation theorem
type_signature: φ preserved under surjective homomorphisms ⟺ equivalent to a positive sentence
description: Lyndon's theorem states that a sentence is preserved under surjective homomorphisms if and only if it is logically equivalent to a positive sentence.

name: Craig interpolation theorem
type_signature: φ ⊨ ψ ⟹ ∃θ in common language with φ⊨θ⊨ψ
description: The Craig interpolation theorem states that whenever one sentence implies another there is an interpolant in their common language implied by the first and implying the second.

name: Beth definability theorem
type_signature: implicit definability ⟹ explicit definability
description: The Beth definability theorem states that a relation implicitly definable in a theory is explicitly definable by a formula in the remaining language.

name: Realizing and omitting types
type_signature: A realizes p if some ā satisfies all of p; omits p otherwise
description: A structure realizes a type when some tuple satisfies every formula in it and omits the type when no tuple does.

name: Countably saturated model
type_signature: realizes every type over every finite parameter set
description: A countably (ℵ₀-) saturated model is one realizing every complete type over each of its finite parameter subsets.

name: ℵ₀-categorical theory
type_signature: T has exactly one countable model up to isomorphism
description: A theory is ℵ₀-categorical when all of its countable models are isomorphic.

name: Oligomorphic permutation group
type_signature: finitely many orbits on A^n for each n
description: A permutation group is oligomorphic when it has only finitely many orbits on n-tuples for every natural number n.

name: Existentially closed structure
type_signature: every existential formula solvable in an extension is already solvable in A
description: A structure is existentially closed in a class when every existential formula with parameters that has a solution in some extension already has a solution in it.

name: Inductive theory
type_signature: models closed under unions of chains; axiomatized by ∀∃ sentences
description: A theory is inductive when the union of any chain of its models is again a model, equivalently when it is axiomatizable by universal-existential sentences.

name: Existence of existentially closed models
type_signature: every model of an inductive theory extends to an e.c. model
description: Every model of an inductive theory embeds into an existentially closed model of the same theory.

name: Model companion / model completion
type_signature: T* mutually model-consistent with T and model-complete
description: The model companion of a theory is a model-complete theory with the same universal consequences, and is a model completion when it additionally has amalgamation over models of the base.

name: Existence and uniqueness of the model companion
type_signature: if a model companion exists it is unique and axiomatizes the e.c. models
description: A theory has at most one model companion, and when it exists it is exactly the theory of the existentially closed models.

name: Quantifier elimination
type_signature: every formula equivalent mod T to a quantifier-free formula
description: A theory has quantifier elimination when every formula is equivalent modulo the theory to a quantifier-free formula in the same free variables.

name: Model-complete with prime model implies QE
type_signature: T model-complete + prime model ⟹ T has quantifier elimination
description: A model-complete theory that has a model embeddable in every model (a prime model) admits quantifier elimination.

name: Nullstellensatz via model completeness
description: This technique derives Hilbert's Nullstellensatz from the model completeness of algebraically closed fields by transferring solvability up to an extension field.

name: Kaiser hull
type_signature: largest inductive theory with the same e.c. models as T
description: The Kaiser hull of a theory is the set of all ∀∃ sentences holding in every existentially closed model, i.e. the largest inductive theory with the same existentially closed models.

name: Stability via type-counting
type_signature: T is λ-stable if |S_n(A)| ≤ λ for all |A| ≤ λ
description: A theory is λ-stable when over every parameter set of size at most λ there are at most λ complete types.

name: Stable / superstable / ω-stable hierarchy
type_signature: ω-stable ⟹ superstable ⟹ stable
description: A theory is stable if it is λ-stable for some λ, superstable if λ-stable for all large λ, and ω-stable if ℵ₀-stable, forming a strict hierarchy.

name: Order property
type_signature: ∃φ(x̄,ȳ) and tuples (ā_i),(b̄_j) with φ(ā_i,b̄_j) ⟺ i<j
description: A theory has the order property when some formula defines an infinite linear order on a sequence of tuples in some model.

name: Indiscernible sequence
type_signature: (a_i)_{i∈I}: tp(a_{i_1},...,a_{i_n}) depends only on the order of indices
description: An indiscernible sequence is an order-indexed family of tuples such that any two increasing tuples of the same length have the same type.

name: Set indiscernibles
type_signature: (a_i): tp of any n distinct elements is the same regardless of order
description: A set of indiscernibles is a family of elements such that every n-element subset realizes the same type irrespective of ordering.

name: Ramsey / Erdős–Rado theorem
type_signature: large enough sets admit monochromatic homogeneous subsets for finite colourings
description: The Ramsey and Erdős–Rado theorems guarantee that any finite colouring of the finite subsets of a sufficiently large set has an infinite homogeneous subset.

name: EM model / functor
type_signature: linear order I ↦ EM(I): model generated by indiscernibles indexed by I
description: The Ehrenfeucht–Mostowski functor sends a linear order to the model generated by an indiscernible sequence of that order type realizing a fixed EM-type.

name: EM construction technique
function_signature: (EM-type, linear order I) → (model with prescribed automorphisms/indiscernibles)
description: The Ehrenfeucht–Mostowski construction builds models with many automorphisms and few types by generating them from indiscernible sequences indexed by a chosen linear order.

name: Forking
type_signature: p(x) over B forks over A⊆B if it implies a disjunction of dividing formulas over A
description: Forking is a notion of dependence under which an extension of a type adds essential new information relative to a smaller parameter set.

name: Heir and coheir (non-forking extensions)
type_signature: heir/coheir: finitely-satisfiable / definable extensions of a type
description: An heir of a type is a coheir-dual extension that is finitely satisfiable in (resp. definable over) the original parameter set, giving canonical non-forking extensions.

name: Prime model over a set (t.t.)
type_signature: prime model of T containing A, existing for totally transcendental T
description: For a totally transcendental theory, the prime model over a parameter set is the least elementary extension containing that set, embedding elementarily into every other model containing it.
